title: Redewendungen: Ich verstehe nur Bahnhof
summary: Twelve German idioms that make zero sense word-for-word — and everything once you know them

blocks.title: Wenn Wörter lügen
blocks.body: Idioms (*Redewendungen*) are where translating word-for-word falls apart. „I only understand train station”? „That's sausage to me”? Nonsense — until you learn the **meaning** as one chunk. These twelve are so common that a native will use them without thinking, so you need to *catch* them.

rows: I don't get a word of it.

blocks.callout: Never translate an idiom part by part. Learn the whole phrase and what it *does*.

blocks.title: Noch sechs für den Alltag
blocks.body: Six more you'll hear constantly — around problems, plans and parties. Notice how many involve **food** (*Wurst, Brei, Bier*) and **animals** (*Schwein, Bär*): German idioms love the kitchen and the farmyard.

rows: to put your foot in it

blocks.title: Tap to hear the top six

items.en: I don't get a word of it.

blocks.explain: *Das ist mir Wurst.* = it's all the same to me / I couldn't care less. Nothing to do with actual sausage — though *egal* is the plain-German version.

blocks.prompt: You didn't catch a single word of the meeting. Which idiom fits?
blocks.explain: *Ich verstehe nur Bahnhof.* — the classic for „I understood nothing.” (Legend traces it to WWI soldiers who only wanted to hear one word: *Bahnhof*, the station home.)

pairs.note: *Ich verstehe nur Bahnhof.* — the literal image is useless; the meaning is everything.
*Schwein haben / Schwein gehabt!* — historically a pig meant wealth, so having one was pure luck.

blocks.prompt: Your friend has a big exam. Wish them luck with the idiom (literally „I press the thumbs”).
blocks.explain: *Ich drück dir die Daumen!* — Germans press their thumbs instead of crossing fingers. *dir* is dative (I press the thumbs *for you*).

blocks.scene: Jonas tells you about his band's chaotic first paid gig — idioms flying.

lines.speaker: Jonas
lines.nl: Ey, gestern der Gig — totales Chaos. Der Verstärker ist ausgefallen.
lines.en: Hey, yesterday's gig — total chaos. The amp died.

lines.speaker: Jonas
lines.nl: Der Typ vom Club redet nur um den heißen Brei. Ich hab nur Bahnhof verstanden.
lines.en: The guy from the club just beat around the bush. I didn't get a word.
lines.spotlight: Two idioms in one line: *um den heißen Brei reden* + *nur Bahnhof verstehen*.

lines.speaker: Jonas
lines.nl: Ja! Am Ende lief's — Schwein gehabt. Da steppte der Bär.
lines.en: Yes! In the end it worked out — lucky us. The place was jumping.
lines.spotlight: *Schwein gehabt* (lucky) + *Da steppt der Bär* (great party) — pure spoken German.

lines.speaker: Jonas
lines.nl: Na ja, halb so viel wie versprochen. Aber das ist mir Wurst — es war geil.
lines.en: Well, half what was promised. But I couldn't care less — it was awesome.

questions.q: Wie war der Gig am Ende?

blocks.prompt: Pick three of today's idioms and, for each, write a short situation where you'd actually say it. Bonus: which one is your favourite, and why?
